LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 6.3.1 COMPARISON OF ADVERBS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we compare things?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs
2. use positive, comparative and superlative degrees of adverbs in sentences
3. appreciate the importance of the correct usage of adverbs

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs

Teach
• Focus skill: identify the degrees of comparison in adverbs.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Comparison of Adverbs
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we compare things?
2. Which words are used to make comparison?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
